solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lawn and elaborate fringes showing gardening ability

parts.note: a lawn is a green, as in a village green or bowling green

indicators.note: to elaborate on something is to work it up into a new form, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A neat lawn and fancy edging show off someone's skill in the garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: someone with a natural talent for making plants grow is said to have this; Americans say green thumb.

clue.text: Rustic friend embraces pioneering stateswoman

indicators.note: the word for friend wraps round the stateswoman, holding her inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend
Nancy Astor was the first woman to take her seat in the British House of Commons

explanation.surface: A country friend hugs a trailblazing female politician.
explanation.walkthrough: Nancy Astor, a Virginia-born American, became the first woman to sit as an MP in Britain's parliament in 1919.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both describe the countryside and simple rural life, as in a shepherds' idyll.

clue.text: Shock as almost attacked by bee

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the word for attacked by bee is dropped

parts.note: someone a bee has attacked has been stung

explanation.surface: Being stung by a bee comes as a nasty surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to shock someone is to daze or stagger them, leaving them unable to react.

clue.text: Parking in exotic Mali next to a leaping antelope

indicators.note: in puts the parking letter inside the reworked country name
exotic suggests something strange and foreign, so the letters of the country are rearranged

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A car park in faraway Mali sits beside a bounding antelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exotic' makes IMAL from MALI; 'in' puts P inside it to give IMPAL, then A follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: this African antelope is famous for its huge bounding leaps when fleeing predators.

clue.text: Medieval soldier is more coarse when receiving singular answer

indicators.note: receiving means the word for more coarse takes the two letters in

parts.note: cruder means more coarse or vulgar
S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

explanation.surface: A knight from the Middle Ages grows ruder when he gets a curt reply.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the medieval Christian warriors who fought the Holy Land campaigns are known by this name.

clue.text: Cutting remark made by hairdresser without hesitation

indicators.note: without means leaving out, so the hesitation sound is removed

parts.note: a barber is a men's hairdresser
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A barber makes a snide comment while cutting, without pausing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a barbed comment is a hurtful jibe, likened to the sharp backward point of an arrowhead.

clue.text: Cook with right hop kiln

parts.note: an oast is a kiln for drying hops, common in Kent

explanation.surface: A brewer uses a hop-drying kiln to prepare food.
explanation.walkthrough: Oast houses, with their cone-shaped roofs, are a familiar sight in the hop-growing county of Kent in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: roasting is one way to cook meat or vegetables in an oven.

clue.text: Tossing and turning, I dream about married female of fantasy

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the shuffled letters go round the abbreviation for married
restless movement in bed suggests the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A restless sleeper dreams of a fantasy woman who is already wed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tossing and turning' turns I DREAM into MERAID; 'about' puts it round M.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a legendary sea creature, half woman and half fish, belongs to folklore and fantasy.

clue.text: Old inebriate's muddled thinking

indicators.note: muddled, as a drunk's head is, says the letters are jumbled

parts.note: inebriate, a drunk, is used as written; the 's is short for is and joins fodder to indicator

explanation.surface: An elderly drunk's thoughts are confused.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: careful thought and consideration before a decision, as a jury does before its verdict.

clue.text: What can be seen in voyages to Niagara's state

indicators.note: what can be seen inside the next words are letters lying within them

explanation.surface: A traveller asks what one sees on trips to Niagara Falls.
explanation.walkthrough: 'state' is a nation here, not an American state, despite Niagara.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a Baltic country and sovereign nation, bordering Latvia and Russia.

clue.text: Prophetess is reflected by lake

indicators.note: reflected, as in a mirror, means the word is is turned round

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for lake, as on maps

explanation.surface: A seer is mirrored in the waters of a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in ancient Greece and Rome a woman who uttered oracles was given this title.

clue.text: One stirring up discontent if going back to market again

indicators.note: going back means the word if is read in reverse

parts.note: to rebrand is to market a product again under a new image

explanation.surface: Someone wonders aloud about returning to a market a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an agitator who stirs up unrest, likened to a burning stick used to light fires.

clue.text: Subtle manoeuvring on railway that's windy

indicators.note: manoeuvring means moving around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Skilful shunting on a railway line on a gusty day.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: weather with strong gusts of wind is described this way.

clue.text: Taxi reversing in backwards

indicators.note: reversing tells you the letters found are read backwards
in says the letters sit inside the following word

explanation.surface: A taxi is reversing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to BAC at the start of 'backwards'; 'reversing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a hired car carrying fare-paying passengers is a cab.

clue.text: Cat is eating fruit, not on plant

indicators.note: eating means the words cat is take the shortened fruit inside them
not means the letters of the word on are left out of the fruit

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: A cat is munching a piece of fruit rather than the plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fruit, not on' is the indicator 'not' with its target 'on', not a fruit that is off; 'eating' wraps 'Cat is' round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a climbing garden plant with large showy flowers, often grown up walls.

clue.text: Tailless African river duck

indicators.note: tailless means the final letter of the river name is cut off

parts.note: the Nile is Africa's longest river

explanation.surface: A bird with no tail swims on an African river.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero, from the egg shape of the nought.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: in cricket a batsman out without scoring makes a duck, meaning nothing or zero.

clue.text: Perhaps don't put on enough lingerie

definitions.meaning: read as a verb, to under-dress is to wear too little: under plus wear
women's intimate garments, worn beneath outer clothing

explanation.surface: Skimpy lingerie that hardly covers anything.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the word as a made-up verb, to wear too little; 'Perhaps' flags that it is whimsical.
explanation.definitionFit: Lingerie is a type of garment worn beneath clothes, close to the skin.

clue.text: Walk slowly from valley, taking in edges of wood

indicators.note: taking in means the valley word holds the edge letters inside it

parts.note: a dale is a valley, as in the Yorkshire Dales

indicators.note: the edges of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Strolling down a valley and through the fringes of a wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to dally or amble along, wasting time on the way.

clue.text: One who's emigrated with retired TV postman

parts.note: ex means former, as one who has retired from a job
Postman Pat is the title character of a British children's TV series

explanation.surface: A well-known TV postman has retired abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: Postman Pat, with his black-and-white cat Jess, is a long-running British children's programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Abbreviation of expatriate: a person who lives outside their native country.

clue.text: Cover with flags: first couple from Panama and Venezuela

indicators.note: first couple means the opening two letters of each country name are taken

explanation.surface: Two Latin American nations drape themselves in national flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to lay a surface with flagstones or paving slabs.

clue.text: Call for battle cry?

parts.note: war is armed conflict, a battle on a large scale
to rant is to shout or cry out wildly

explanation.surface: A rallying call to fight, a battle cry.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'Call for battle cry' reads as one phrase, a war cry, but splits differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a situation that calls for action justifies or merits it.

clue.text: Wander about Italian capital, speaking

indicators.note: speaking means the city name is spoken, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A tourist strolls around the Italian capital, chatting.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to roam is to travel aimlessly or drift from place to place.

clue.text: Teasingly reveals a number

indicators.note: teasing out or teasing fibres separates and rearranges them, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone coyly discloses a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: more than two but not many, an indefinite number of things.

clue.text: A Russian fighter meets old Spanish friend

parts.note: the MiG is a Russian fighter jet

explanation.surface: A Russian jet encounters a former Spanish ally.
explanation.definitionFit: Loanword: Spanish for a friend or pal, widely used in English.
